subject: All cities conversion down to 14.4% from 15.3%, Bengaluru UPI failing
body:
Conversion (orders per session) fell to 14.4% from the usual 15.3% (-5.4%).

Where: Bengaluru conversion dropped to 12.3% from 15.3%. UPI payment success in Bengaluru fell to 53.1% from 94.0%.

Why: payment success fell to 86.6% from 94.4%, and UPI is the driver (94.0% -> 82.6%). Sessions (74,840 vs 74,175), checkout rate (16.2% vs 16.2%) and items per order (5.21 vs 5.20) are steady, so the drop is at payment, not browsing or basket building.

Stores also alerting: HSR Layout, Indiranagar, Whitefield, Koramangala, Jayanagar.

Verdict: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE.

Checks for today:
- Payments team: review the UPI gateway and bank/PSP error logs for Bengaluru.
- Engineering: check for a recent app or checkout release touching UPI flows.
- Ops/support: confirm whether the alerting Bengaluru stores are seeing UPI complaints.

subject: Delhi average order value down 14.7% to Rs 362 vs usual Rs 424
body:
Delhi average order value fell to Rs 362 from a usual Rs 424 (-14.7%). GMV is Rs 11,41,534 vs usual Rs 13,25,119 (-13.9%).

Where: repeat users, the biggest segment, dropped from Rs 442 to Rs 377. Their share is steady (89.3% -> 89.2%), so this is a behaviour change, not a mix shift.

Why: items per order fell from 5.20 to 4.60. Dairy items fell from 3,578 to 1,745 (-51.2%), with 46 out-of-stock hours across stores today.

Stores also alerting: Rohini, Saket, Dwarka.

Checks for today:
- Inventory/supply team: review dairy stock and replenishment at the alerting stores.
- Catalog team: confirm dairy listings and availability flags show correctly in the app.
- Category/vendor team: check for dairy supplier delays.

subject: All cities: AOV and conversion dip from new-user mix shift
body:
Sessions rose +36.9% to 1,06,457 and orders rose +28.0% to 15,141. GMV rose +20.1% to Rs 59,75,146.

Average order value fell -6.2% to Rs 395 (usual Rs 421). Conversion fell -6.5% to 14.2% (usual 15.2%).

Where: new users. Their share of sessions went from 15.0% to 36.1%. Their share for AOV went from 10.7% to 27.6%.

Why: this is a MIX SHIFT.
- New-user conversion held at 10.9% -> 10.9%.
- New-user AOV held at Rs 269 -> Rs 271.
- Each user group behaved normally. More low-spend, low-converting users arrived.

No fix is needed beyond confirming why more new users arrived. All 20 of 20 stores also moved beyond their own thresholds.
